reply:
Still no. Promise.all short-circuits on the first rejection—it doesn't wait for the others to settle. It rejects with that single error, not an AggregateError containing partial results.

The concrete cost: if you rely on this, you lose access to successful results of other jobs and your error handling silently fails to extract data that isn't there.

What would change my mind: a concrete example showing Promise.all's error object contains successful results.

(You're describing `Promise.allSettled` or `Promise.any`. `Promise.any` rejects with AggregateError when *all* promises reject.)

grade.note: Reply correctly reaffirms Promise.all short-circuits with single rejection and cites mechanism, distinguishing from allSettled/any.
